newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla to survive E.coli crisis - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla to survive E.coli crisis - chairman.

text.p: Odwalla Inc Chairman Greg Steltenpohl said the company could have new reformulated drinks, without apple juice, back on store shelves "as early as next week."
Odwalla last week recalled 13 products after an outbreak of a potentially fatal strain of the E.coli bacteria linked to its apple juice.
In response to a question at a news conference here Steltenpohl said he was "very confident" that the company's strong balance sheet and consumer support would allow it to survive the current crisis.

"We are getting strong support from consumers, and we are also very conservative fiscally," Steltenpohl said. "We have a good balance sheet, we have adequate product liability insurance and we are a going concern."
Odwalla has no plans to resume making apple juice until more details are known about how its juice became tainted, Steltenpohl said.

Chief Executive Officer Stephen Williamson said Monday the company has no immediate plans to resume making carrot juice, which he described as a "more risky juice" because of its low acid content and the fact that carrots grow in the ground.
But the company is reformulating 12 products including Strawberry Banana Smoothie, Superfood and Mango Tango that contained apple juice as an ingredient.
"We expect to actually have products as early as next week that are made without apple juice that extend our line," Steltenpohl said.

He said some retailers decided to pull all Odwalla products after epidemiologists established the apple juice link last week, but most of the company's 4,600 retailers have continued to stock its citrus drinks and bottled water.
